judgements.reason: Bridge -> Reasoning. `given` asserts "Export control is a mature enforcement instrument; model-distillation has no equivalent statute", and two bridges this week attack both halves. The 2026-07-26 bridge (validation.92ea7a5157b125ad) carries NYT reporting that Washington's preferred mechanism is deliberately NOT a docketed instrument - "sanctions, procurement pressure and soft signalling assembled into a slow-motion ban rather than announced as one", leaving "no single instrument a self-hoster can read and comply with" - which undercuts the inference from mature machinery to the `so_that`/`landing` requirement of a publicly filed action naming Moonshot or the Thailand route. The 2026-07-28 bridge (validation.51a5d1c91b207ab3) then records Treasury Secretary Bessent warning Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over intellectual-property theft - a named instrument pointed at the distillation half, which is the prediction's own second falsifier. Reframe `given` to distinguish "has an instrument" from "will use a filed instrument", and acknowledge that a sanctions track now exists on the provenance side. `because` remains accurate as historical fact.

Fix is a re-score of 2026-07-28, not a rewrite - escalate rather than auto-apply. Note also that support_direction is 100% 'support' with contradiction_score 0.0 across all 8258 evidence links repo-wide, so the 07-26 and 07-28 counter-signals above are invisible to any automated contradiction check.

(1) need_task.b531f05014db14a6 (Need actor "US sanctions designation officer, Treasury OFAC") has how_text NULL while status='open'; the needs_tasks schema comment states the orchestrator marks status='blocked' when the 5W1H extraction is partial. 17 partial rows exist repo-wide and 0 are blocked, so the rule is unimplemented. The consequence here is that the Need runway closes 2026-12-31, six months BEFORE this prediction's landing window (2027-01-01..2027-06-30) opens, so no Need can ever overlap its own landing. Content is otherwise coherent; escalate the parser and the blocked-status rule rather than rewriting text. Cross-stream: the 07-28 bridge points the OFAC actor at the distillation charge rather than the Thailand route this Need describes.

Bridge -> Reasoning, on both `because` and `given`. The 2026-07-30 bridge (validation.9d04fd325ceba399) carries Unit 42's first reconstruction of an open-weight model - DeepSeek wired into the Hermes Agent framework - running an offensive campaign with no human in the loop: enumeration across ten product families, PoC retrieval, FOFA target discovery, version checks and attempted exploitation, with Unit 42 concluding a functional end-to-end autonomous offensive capability. That makes `because` ("OpenAI's own models chained a real zero-day to autonomous RCE") historical rather than the live precondition, and moves the open gap from AUTONOMY to EFFICACY - every exploit the agent attempted failed, and the actual breaches were by hand. `given` is worse off: it claims the mechanism is "anyone can fine-tune out refusals", but the observed operator did no de-alignment at all - the same bridge and validation.50650b2e4ae81cd8 record OpenAI refusing his requests and disabling his account, after which he simply switched to a model that never refused. The real mechanism is model substitution, not refusal removal. Also reframe against validation.a451d0ab93c7e9ca (07-26: open-weight Kimi K3 driving 32 agents to 19 Redis zero-days and a 27-minute authenticated RCE PoC) and validation.acc41140f80c524d (07-29: Hugging Face published the full step-indexed 17,600-action chain, a public blueprint a reproducer can work from).

Bridge -> Reasoning. `given` names grid interconnection as the binding constraint and `so_that` expects a second lab to copy the self-financed structure, but the 2026-07-27 bridge (validation.8270b709dcd9facf) has the originator of the template doing the opposite at larger scale: OpenAI's ten-gigawatt Piketon campus is a LEASE from SoftBank-backed SB Energy, with NVIDIA reportedly asked to guarantee roughly $250bn behind it because OpenAI holds no investment-grade credit rating, and NVIDIA's SK Group letter of intent runs the same vendor-anchored way. That introduces a second binding constraint the reasoning does not mention - counterparty credit - which pushes toward leasing and vendor guarantees rather than lab-funded interconnection. The 2026-07-28 bridge (validation.64f9ea8fe72ab143) compounds it: FCC action on connected power inverters narrows the supplier list for a lab that funds its own grid hardware, raising the cost of exactly the route this prediction expects to spread. Reframe `given` to weigh interconnection against financing structure, and state why a second lab would self-finance when the first is leasing.

Bridge -> Reasoning: `given` took two independent counter-cases in one week. It claims "Fix cadence is automating while identifier assignment stays human-paced and request-driven". The 2026-07-28 bridge (validation.4c45723536f64ffc) records both of that day's vulnerabilities arriving fully labelled - CVE-2026-16812 at CVSS 10.0 with named fixed builds, a KEV entry and a three-day federal patch clock, and CVE-2026-53264 at CVSS 7.8 backported to seven stable lines - and the bridge itself flags the second as awkward, because a seven-branch backport is exactly the cadence the claim expects identifiers to fall behind, and identification kept up. The 2026-07-30 bridge (validation.a85bd5714ef4f884) is sharper still: Ruflo shipped a fix within 24 hours of disclosure carrying CVE-2026-59726, a CVSS 10.0 and a vendor-assigned name - fast fix and complete labelling on the same event. Reframe `given` away from "assignment cannot keep up" toward the narrower and still-supported mechanism the 07-30 bridge points at: Redis's own publication sequencing, plus unscored defaults (the unauthenticated MongoDB that bridge notes) that the identifier system never covers. `because` (the July 23 seven-branch release) stands as fact.

Bridge -> Reasoning on both `because` and `given`. `given` states "Refusal filters key on content, not on who asks, so they bind the responder and not the intruder" - and the 2026-07-30 bridge (validation.50650b2e4ae81cd8) records the opposite from Unit 42: OpenAI's safety systems refused the knaithe operator's policy-violating requests and disabled the account linked to the activity, i.e. refusal bound the intruder, and bound him BY ACCOUNT rather than by content, which is exactly the mechanism `given` says refusal filters lack. The bridge draws the conclusion explicitly, that this weakens the case for exemptions rather than strengthening it. Separately `because` omits known prior art surfaced by the 2026-07-26 bridge (validation.0451730d678a8dd3): a tiered-access program for defenders was already named in a post dated December 10, 2025 - seven months before the intrusion the `because` cites - with nothing enrollable behind it. Rewrite both cells; `so_that` and `landing` can stand.
